title: Frequently Asked Questions
subtitle: Everything you need to know about shipping your vehicle with Y7 Logistics.

items.q: How does auto transport work?
items.a: We match you with licensed, insured carriers through Central Dispatch. You request a quote, we find the best carrier, they pick up and deliver your vehicle door-to-door.

items.q: How long does shipping take?
items.a: 1–3 days for routes under 500 miles, 3–7 days coast-to-coast. Times are estimates — weather, traffic, and carrier availability can affect transit.

items.q: What information do I need to get a quote?
items.a: Vehicle year/make/model or VIN, pickup and delivery cities, and your preferred dates. For auction vehicles, the lot number helps too.

items.q: Do I need to be present for pickup/delivery?
items.a: Someone 18+ must be present to inspect the vehicle and sign the Bill of Lading (BOL) at both pickup and delivery.

items.q: How much does it cost to ship a car?
items.a: Prices depend on distance, vehicle size, transport type (open vs enclosed), and market conditions. Request a quote for an accurate estimate.

items.q: Are there hidden fees?
items.a: No. Your quote includes everything. Inoperable vehicles may have an additional $100–300 fee disclosed upfront.

items.q: What payment methods do you accept?
items.a: Zelle, bank transfer, ACH for prepayment. Cash or certified funds to the carrier for COD at delivery.

items.q: Do you require a deposit?
items.a: Depends on the payment method. Prepaid orders are paid in full before dispatch. COD orders may require a booking deposit.

items.q: How do I track my vehicle?
items.a: Through our customer portal, Telegram bot (@y7dispatch_bot), or email updates at every stage.

items.q: What insurance coverage is included?
items.a: Every carrier in our network carries a minimum of $100,000 in cargo insurance — most carry $250,000 or more. This is a Y7 verification requirement; we confirm active coverage through Central Dispatch before assigning any load.

items.q: What if my car is damaged?
items.a: Note any new damage on the BOL at delivery. File a claim within 24 hours with photos. We help coordinate with the carrier’s insurance.

items.q: What is a Bill of Lading (BOL)?
items.a: A legal document recording your vehicle’s condition at pickup and delivery. Always inspect and sign it carefully.

items.q: Do you pick up from IAAI, Copart, Manheim?
items.a: Yes. We handle gate passes, lot releases, and all auction paperwork.

items.q: What is a gate pass?
items.a: A document from the auction authorizing vehicle release. You can upload it through our portal or Telegram bot.

items.q: Which US ports do you deliver to?
items.a: Newark NJ, Houston TX, Savannah GA, Baltimore MD, Los Angeles CA, Jacksonville FL, and more.

items.q: What documents are needed for port delivery?
items.a: Title or export documentation, gate pass (if from auction), and any port-specific release forms.

items.q: Do you offer volume discounts?
items.a: Yes. Dealers and exporters shipping 10+ vehicles/month qualify for custom pricing with a dedicated dispatcher.

items.q: What is your transparent pricing model?
items.a: For exporters: carrier rate at cost + our flat service fee. No markups on transport.

items.q: Can I get a dedicated dispatcher?
items.a: Yes, for volume accounts (10+ vehicles/month). One point of contact for all your shipments.

items.q: How do I contact Y7 if I do not use phone calls?
items.a: Y7 customer support is digital-first. You can reach us through the Client Portal, Telegram bot (@y7dispatch_bot), or email (info@y7agency.com for new inquiries, dispatch@y7agency.com for active shipments). Every request is logged in writing, documents are trackable, and multi-order coordination is easy. Existing customers have 24/7 access via the portal and Telegram bot for shipment-related urgent matters.

items.q: How does the driver coordinate delivery with me?
items.a: After your carrier is assigned, the driver's direct phone number appears in your portal. The driver will call you 1-4 hours before pickup and delivery to confirm timing, directions, and unload point. This is standard practice for all auto transport — physical delivery logistics require real-time voice coordination that can't happen through text alone.

items.q: How do I receive documents like the Bill of Lading?
items.a: All documents are handled digitally. The BOL is signed at pickup and delivery (paper or e-signature depending on carrier), then uploaded to your portal within 24 hours. Photos of the vehicle's condition at both touchpoints are attached. Invoices, receipts, and insurance proof are emailed and also stored in your portal for permanent access.
